title: Influence of osteopathic treatment on systemic inflammatory activity in different age groups
summary:
The plan is to investigate the influence of osteopathic treatments on blood levels of inflammatory substances and to determine heart rate variability, comparing a young and an older population group. Initially, only participants without significant pre-existing conditions will be examined.
The aim is to examine whether direct and indirect manual mobilization of the vagus nerve has a direct influence on inflammatory activity. In older people, the declining function of the vagus nerve is believed to be responsible for an increase in diseases of the nervous system in old age. A positive influence through manual treatment could provide meaningful support for these diseases (e.g., dementia or Parkinson's disease).
On 6 dates at weekly intervals (5 treatments) and a subsequent treatment after a further 4-8 weeks, blood samples will be taken before and after the treatment, heart rate variability will be determined, and a questionnaire will be completed befre the first and after the last treatment.
conditions: Healthy subjects under the age of 30 and over the age of 60 who are in good health, in particular those with no previous immunological or rheumatic diseases or operations in the treatment region, will be examined.

interventions.name: 23 subjects under the age of 30 and 23 subjects aged 60 and over undergo blood sampling for testing for IL-1, TNF-alpha, IL-10 and determination of heart rate variability, osteopathic examination and specific treatment of the vagus nerve in the head and neck area. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Younger adults between 18 and under 30 years of age (group 1). Older adults over 59 and under 80 years of age (group 2).
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria are chronic inflammation, rheumatic diseases, malignant diseases in the medical history, previous surgery (head and neck surgery, kidney and adrenal gland surgery, brain and spinal cord surgery, any surgery that causes vegetative symptoms, such as major abdominal or thoracic surgery), no free direction during examination (osteopathic red flag), and medication with immunosuppressants
(including corticosteroids, tocilizumab, sarilumab, anti-TNF, JAK inhibitors, methotrexate, leflunomide, hydroxychloroquine, chloroquine) and a history of vasovagal syncope. Audible cardiac arrhythmias such as atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, arrhythmias.
